1.1.1.1.body:
Who Needs GST Registration?

GST registration may be mandatory or voluntary depending on the nature of your business, annual turnover, and business activities. Our team evaluates your business profile and advises the most suitable registration approach.

Businesses that commonly require GST registration include:

  • Businesses crossing the prescribed turnover threshold.
  • Businesses involved in interstate supply of goods or services.
  • E-commerce sellers and marketplace vendors.
  • Importers and exporters.
  • Service providers operating across multiple states.
  • Businesses liable under reverse charge provisions.
  • Casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons.
  • Businesses opting for voluntary GST registration to claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) and improve business credibility.

Documents Commonly Required for GST Registration

The required documentation varies depending on the type of business entity. Commonly required documents include:

  • PAN Card of the applicant or business entity.
  • Aadhaar Card of promoters or authorised signatories.
  • Business address proof.
  • Identity and address proof of promoters, partners, or directors.
  • Passport-size photographs.
  • Certificate of Incorporation, Partnership Deed, LLP Agreement, or Trust Deed (where applicable).
  • Board Resolution or Authorisation Letter (for companies and LLPs).
  • Bank account proof.

1.1.1.2.plainBody:
GST return filing is a crucial compliance requirement for every registered taxpayer under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime. Businesses are required to file different GST returns based on their registration type, turnover, and business activities. Timely and accurate GST return filing ensures compliance with statutory requirements, enables seamless Input Tax Credit (ITC) claims, and helps businesses avoid interest, penalties, and notices from tax authorities.

At Ritesh Arora & Associates, we provide comprehensive GST return filing services for businesses across diverse industries and entity types. Our professionals assist with preparing, reviewing, and filing GST returns while ensuring complete accuracy and compliance with the latest GST regulations. Whether you are a regular taxpayer, composition dealer, e-commerce operator, Input Service Distributor (ISD), or non-resident taxable person, we simplify the entire return filing process so you can focus on growing your business.

From monthly and quarterly GST returns to annual returns and final returns after cancellation of GST registration, our team manages every aspect of GST compliance with precision and timely execution.

Our GST Return Filing Services

We provide end-to-end GST return filing solutions designed to help businesses remain compliant throughout the financial year.

Preparation of GST Returns

We collect and review your financial records, sales invoices, purchase invoices, Input Tax Credit details, and tax liability to prepare accurate GST returns in accordance with applicable regulations.

Monthly & Quarterly GST Return Filing

Our professionals prepare and file monthly or quarterly GST returns based on your business category, turnover, and applicable filing scheme, ensuring every return is submitted before the prescribed due date.

Annual GST Return Filing

We prepare and file annual GST returns by reconciling financial records, GST returns, and Input Tax Credit details to ensure complete statutory compliance.

Input Tax Credit Reconciliation

Our team performs detailed reconciliation of purchase records with GST portal data to identify mismatches, maximize eligible Input Tax Credit, and minimize compliance risks.

GST Notices & Query Assistance

If discrepancies arise or notices are issued by the GST department, we assist in preparing appropriate responses, rectifying errors, and ensuring timely compliance with departmental requirements.

GST Return Amendments

Where corrections or revisions are permitted under GST regulations, we assist businesses in making the necessary amendments while ensuring proper documentation and statutory compliance.

Types of GST Returns We Handle

Different categories of taxpayers are required to file different GST returns depending on their business activities and registration status. Our experts assist with filing all major GST returns accurately and within the prescribed timelines.

GSTR-1

Filed by regular taxpayers to report outward supplies of goods and services. It may be filed monthly or quarterly depending on the taxpayer's turnover and eligibility under the QRMP Scheme.

GSTR-3B

A summary return used for reporting tax liability and making GST payments. Businesses file this return either monthly or quarterly based on their applicable filing scheme.

GSTR-4

Filed annually by Composition Scheme taxpayers to report business turnover and tax liability under the Composition Scheme.

GSTR-5

Filed by non-resident taxable persons to report taxable transactions undertaken during their period of registration in India.

GSTR-6

Filed by Input Service Distributors (ISDs) for distributing eligible Input Tax Credit among different branches or units of an organization.

GSTR-7

Filed monthly by government departments and other notified entities responsible for deducting Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) under GST.

GSTR-8

Filed by e-commerce operators responsible for collecting Tax Collected at Source (TCS) and reporting TCS collected from suppliers.

GSTR-9

The annual return filed by eligible regular taxpayers, providing a consolidated summary of outward supplies, inward supplies, tax payments, and Input Tax Credit for the financial year.

GSTR-9A

Filed by composition taxpayers where applicable under the relevant GST regulations for the financial year.

GSTR-9C

Filed by taxpayers liable for GST audit. It includes reconciliation between audited financial statements and GST returns along with certification by a Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant.

GSTR-10

The final return filed by businesses cancelling their GST registration within the prescribed time limit to complete the cancellation process and avoid penalties.

Why Timely GST Return Filing Matters

Filing GST returns within the prescribed due dates is essential for maintaining compliance and avoiding unnecessary financial and legal consequences.

• Avoid interest, late fees, and statutory penalties.

• Ensure uninterrupted Input Tax Credit claims.

• Maintain a positive GST compliance rating.

• Reduce the risk of departmental notices and assessments.

• Facilitate smooth business operations and vendor compliance.

• Maintain accurate financial records throughout the year.

• Support hassle-free annual reconciliations and audits.

Our GST Return Filing Process

Our systematic approach ensures every GST return is filed accurately and within the applicable due dates.

Step 1: Data Collection

We collect sales data, purchase records, tax invoices, Input Tax Credit details, and other relevant financial information required for GST return preparation.

Step 2: Review & Reconciliation

Our professionals review all transactions, reconcile Input Tax Credit, and identify discrepancies before filing the return.

Step 3: Return Preparation

We prepare the applicable GST returns based on your business category, registration type, and statutory filing requirements.

Step 4: Filing on GST Portal

After verification and approval, the returns are filed electronically through the GST portal within the prescribed due dates.

Step 5: Post-Filing Support

We provide filing acknowledgements, assist with departmental queries if any arise, and offer continuous compliance support for future return filings.

Our GST Advisory Services

We provide practical GST advisory solutions that help businesses remain compliant while improving tax efficiency and reducing unnecessary risks.

Classification & Tax Structure Advisory

Correct classification of goods and services is essential for determining the applicable GST rate. We assist businesses in identifying the appropriate HSN and SAC codes, determining the correct tax structure, and minimizing the risk of incorrect classification that could result in future disputes, notices, or additional tax liabilities.

Valuation & Transaction Advisory

Determining the correct transaction value is critical for GST compliance. We advise businesses on valuation principles, related-party transactions, reimbursements, discounts, inclusions, exclusions, and other valuation matters to ensure transactions comply with GST provisions and withstand regulatory scrutiny.

Place of Supply Analysis

GST liability often depends on determining the correct place of supply. Our experts analyze business transactions involving goods and services to establish whether GST should be treated as intra-state or inter-state, helping businesses apply the correct tax treatment and avoid compliance issues.

Input Tax Credit (ITC) Optimization

Input Tax Credit represents a significant opportunity for reducing tax costs when managed correctly. We help businesses maximize eligible ITC claims by reviewing purchase transactions, identifying blocked credits, managing reversals, and implementing reconciliation practices that ensure compliance with GST regulations.

Return Planning & Compliance Advisory

Effective GST compliance requires more than timely filing. We provide strategic guidance on return planning, filing schedules, reconciliation procedures, and compliance monitoring to help businesses minimize mismatches, avoid penalties, and maintain accurate GST records throughout the financial year.

Compliance System Setup & Record Management

A strong compliance framework reduces operational risks and improves reporting accuracy. We assist businesses in implementing internal GST controls, maintaining statutory records, developing documentation procedures, and establishing compliance systems that support efficient return filing and future audits.

Liaison with Tax Authorities

Businesses frequently receive clarifications, notices, or information requests from GST authorities. Our professionals assist in preparing responses, providing supporting documentation, handling pre-audit communications, and representing businesses during compliance-related interactions with tax authorities.

Periodic Reviews & GST Health Checks

Regular GST reviews help businesses identify compliance gaps before they become major issues. We conduct periodic GST health checks, review existing compliance practices, evaluate risk areas, recommend corrective measures, and help businesses stay aligned with the latest regulatory requirements.

Why GST Advisory is Important

With GST laws continuously evolving, businesses require ongoing professional guidance to remain compliant while making informed financial and operational decisions. Effective GST advisory helps businesses improve compliance, reduce unnecessary tax exposure, and strengthen overall financial governance.

• Interpret complex GST laws with confidence.

• Reduce the risk of tax disputes and departmental notices.

• Optimize Input Tax Credit and improve cash flow.

• Ensure correct tax treatment for business transactions.

1.2.1.2.1.body:
Form 24Q – TDS on Salary Payments

Form 24Q is filed by employers who deduct tax from salaries paid to employees. It contains details relating to employee salaries, tax deductions, exemptions claimed, deductions under various sections, and taxes deposited during the financial year.

This form is applicable to:

  1. Companies and corporate employers.
  2. Partnership firms and LLPs employing staff.
  3. Proprietorship businesses.
  4. Startups and growing organisations.
  5. Any employer responsible for deducting TDS on salary.

Our services include:

  1. Preparation and filing of quarterly Form 24Q.
  2. Verification of salary details and tax computations.
  3. Reconciliation with payroll records.
  4. Generation of accurate Form 16.
  5. Correction of filing errors and revised returns where required.

Accurate filing of Form 24Q helps employees receive proper tax credit and minimises the risk of mismatch notices from the Income Tax Department.

Form 26Q – TDS on Domestic Non-Salary Payments

Form 26Q is applicable when tax is deducted on payments made to resident individuals or entities, other than salary. It is one of the most commonly filed TDS returns and covers various business and professional transactions.

Typical payments covered include:

  1. Professional and consultancy fees.
  2. Contractor and subcontractor payments.
  3. Rent payments.
  4. Commission and brokerage.
  5. Interest payments.
  6. Director remuneration and other specified payments.

This form is commonly filed by:

  1. Individuals and proprietorship concerns.
  2. Partnership firms.
  3. Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs).
  4. Private Limited Companies.
  5. Public Limited Companies.
  6. Trusts and other organisations making specified payments.

Our services include:

  1. Verification of TDS applicability.
  2. Preparation and filing of Form 26Q.
  3. Validation of deductee information.
  4. Reconciliation of challans and tax payments.
  5. Filing correction statements wherever necessary.

Timely and accurate filing ensures deductees receive proper credit in Form 26AS and reduces the likelihood of departmental notices.

Form 27Q – TDS on Payments to Non-Residents

Form 27Q is required when tax is deducted on payments made to non-residents or foreign companies. Such transactions involve additional compliance requirements due to the applicability of Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAA), withholding tax provisions, and international taxation rules.

Common payments covered include:

  1. Royalty payments.
  2. Fees for technical services.
  3. Overseas consultancy charges.
  4. Interest paid to foreign lenders.
  5. Other taxable payments to non-residents.

Our services include:

  1. Determination of applicable withholding tax rates.
  2. DTAA eligibility review.
  3. Preparation and filing of Form 27Q.
  4. Verification of supporting documentation.
  5. Compliance with international tax reporting requirements.
  6. Assistance in responding to departmental queries.

Proper filing of Form 27Q helps businesses avoid disputes relating to international tax compliance and ensures adherence to cross-border taxation requirements.

1.2.1.2.3.body:
Form 24Q – TDS on Salary Payments

Form 24Q is filed by employers who deduct tax at source on salaries paid to employees. The return contains detailed information regarding employee salary, exemptions claimed, deductions allowed, tax deducted, and taxes deposited during the quarter.

This form is applicable to:

  1. Companies and corporate employers.
  2. Partnership Firms and LLPs employing staff.
  3. Proprietorship businesses.
  4. Startups and MSMEs.
  5. Government departments and other organisations paying salaries.

Our services include:

  1. Preparation and quarterly filing of Form 24Q.
  2. Verification of payroll records and salary computations.
  3. Reconciliation of TDS deducted with challan payments.
  4. Assistance in generating accurate Form 16 for employees.
  5. Filing correction statements wherever necessary.

Proper filing of Form 24Q ensures that employees receive accurate TDS credit and helps employers avoid compliance issues.

Form 26Q – TDS on Domestic Non-Salary Payments

Form 26Q is used to report TDS deducted on payments made to resident individuals and entities other than salary. It is one of the most frequently filed TDS returns and covers various business and professional payments.

Common transactions covered include:

  1. Professional and consultancy fees.
  2. Contractor and subcontractor payments.
  3. Rent.
  4. Commission and brokerage.
  5. Interest payments.
  6. Director remuneration.
  7. Other payments liable for TDS under the Income Tax Act.

This form is commonly filed by:

  1. Individuals and Proprietorships.
  2. Partnership Firms.
  3. Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs).
  4. Private Limited Companies.
  5. Public Limited Companies.
  6. Trusts and other organisations making specified payments.

Our assistance includes:

  1. Determining TDS applicability.
  2. Preparation and filing of Form 26Q.
  3. Verification of deductee details and challan information.
  4. Filing revised and correction statements where required.
  5. Reconciliation with Form 26AS and TRACES records.

Timely and accurate filing helps deductees receive proper tax credit while reducing the possibility of departmental notices.

Form 27Q – TDS on Payments to Non-Residents

Form 27Q is applicable when tax is deducted on payments made to non-residents or foreign companies. Such transactions involve additional compliance requirements due to international taxation provisions, Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs), and withholding tax rules.

Typical payments covered include:

  1. Royalty.
  2. Fees for technical services.
  3. Overseas consultancy charges.
  4. Interest paid to foreign lenders.
  5. Other taxable payments made to non-residents.

Our services include:

  1. Determining the applicable withholding tax rate.
  2. Reviewing DTAA eligibility and treaty benefits.
  3. Preparation and filing of Form 27Q.
  4. Verification of supporting documents and tax residency records.
  5. Assistance in complying with international tax reporting requirements.
  6. Support during departmental assessments and notices.

Our professionals ensure that cross-border transactions comply with Indian tax laws while reducing the risk of tax disputes and penalties.

1.2.1.3.plainBody:
Advance Tax is the income tax payable in installments during the financial year instead of a single payment at the end of the year. It is applicable to taxpayers whose estimated tax liability exceeds the prescribed threshold under the Income Tax Act, 1961. Accurate computation of advance tax is essential to avoid interest under Sections 234B and 234C, ensure timely compliance, and effectively manage cash flow.

At Ritesh Arora & Associates, we provide comprehensive Advance Tax Computation services for individuals, professionals, businesses, LLPs, companies, and other taxable entities. Our professionals carefully estimate your annual tax liability, reconcile available tax credits, and prepare a structured payment plan to help you remain fully compliant while avoiding unnecessary interest and penalties.

Our Advance Tax Computation Services

Detailed Income Projection

Accurate advance tax begins with a realistic estimate of your annual taxable income. We analyse all relevant sources of income to determine your expected tax liability for the financial year.

Our income projection covers:

Salary income.

Business or professional income.

Capital gains.

Rental income.

Interest income.

Dividend income.

Income from other sources.

This comprehensive evaluation helps ensure that advance tax is calculated accurately based on your expected earnings.

Quarterly Advance Tax Calculation

Advance tax must be paid in prescribed installments during the financial year. We compute the tax payable for each due date after considering your projected income and applicable tax provisions.

Our services include:

Computation of quarterly advance tax liability.

Calculation of tax payable for June, September, December, and March installments.

Review of revised income estimates during the year.

Assistance in generating tax payment challans.

Guidance on timely payment to avoid interest and late charges.

Adjustment of TDS, TCS & Previous Tax Payments

To prevent excess tax payments, it is important to consider taxes already deducted or collected at source before computing advance tax liability.

We assist in:

Reconciliation of Form 26AS.

Review of the Annual Information Statement (AIS).

Verification of Taxpayer Information Summary (TIS).

Adjustment of TDS credits.

Adjustment of TCS credits.

Consideration of self-assessment tax and previous advance tax payments.

This ensures that only the actual balance tax liability is paid.

Interest Liability Analysis (Sections 234B & 234C)

Incorrect estimation or delayed payment of advance tax may attract interest under Sections 234B and 234C of the Income Tax Act. We proactively analyse your tax position to identify any potential shortfalls and recommend corrective measures before interest liabilities arise.

Our analysis includes:

Review of installment-wise tax payments.

Identification of shortfalls or deferred payments.

Estimation of interest exposure.

Guidance on corrective tax payments where necessary.

Tax Optimisation Before the Financial Year Ends

Advance tax planning is also an opportunity to optimise your overall tax liability through legitimate tax-saving measures. Our professionals review your financial position and recommend suitable planning strategies based on applicable tax provisions.

Our advisory includes:

Identification of eligible deductions and exemptions.

Review of tax-saving investments.

Planning for capital gains and business income.

Set-off of eligible losses.

Selection of the appropriate tax regime, wherever applicable.

Strategic year-end tax planning to improve overall tax efficiency.

Benefits of Professional Advance Tax Planning

Proper advance tax planning offers several financial and compliance advantages, including:

Accurate estimation of tax liability.

Timely compliance with statutory due dates.

Reduced risk of interest under Sections 234B and 234C.

Better cash flow planning throughout the financial year.

Optimised utilisation of available tax credits.

Improved tax efficiency through proactive planning.

Reduced risk of notices and tax disputes.

Complete compliance with the provisions of the Income Tax Act.

Our Advance Tax Computation Process

Step

Our Approach

Income Assessment

Review all expected sources of income for the financial year.

Tax Computation

Calculate estimated tax liability after considering deductions, exemptions, and applicable tax regime.

Credit Reconciliation

Adjust TDS, TCS, and previous tax payments using Form 26AS, AIS, and TIS.

Installment Planning

Compute quarterly advance tax payable for each due date.

Year-End Review

Reassess income estimates and recommend tax optimisation strategies before the close of the financial year.

Plan Your Taxes with Confidence

Advance tax is not just a statutory obligation,it is an essential part of effective financial planning. With accurate forecasting, timely tax payments, and proactive tax optimisation, businesses and individuals can minimise interest costs, improve cash flow management, and remain fully compliant with the Income Tax Act. Our Advance Tax Computation services provide practical guidance and reliable support, helping you manage your tax obligations efficiently throughout the financial year.

1.2.1.4.plainBody:
Income Computation and Disclosure Standards (ICDS) are a set of tax accounting standards notified by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) under the Income Tax Act, 1961. These standards prescribe the manner in which certain categories of income and expenses should be recognised for the purpose of computing taxable income. ICDS generally applies to taxpayers following the mercantile system of accounting and is intended to bring uniformity and consistency in tax reporting.

Improper application of ICDS may result in tax adjustments, scrutiny assessments, additional tax liabilities, and prolonged litigation. At Ritesh Arora & Associates, we provide comprehensive ICDS advisory services to help businesses understand the applicability of these standards, align their accounting practices with tax requirements, and ensure accurate computation of taxable income.

Our ICDS Advisory Services

Applicability Assessment

The first step towards ICDS compliance is determining whether the standards apply to your business or professional income. Our professionals carefully evaluate your accounting method, business structure, and nature of transactions to assess the applicability of ICDS provisions.

Our assessment includes:

Review of the accounting system followed by the taxpayer.

Evaluation of business and professional income.

Determination of applicable ICDS provisions.

Identification of compliance requirements based on the nature of operations.

Review of Accounting Policies for Tax Alignment

Accounting policies adopted for financial reporting may differ from those prescribed under ICDS for tax computation. We review your existing accounting practices to identify areas where adjustments may be required for tax purposes.

Our services include:

Review of accounting methods and policies.

Comparison between financial reporting standards and ICDS requirements.

Identification of accounting treatments requiring tax adjustments.

Recommendations for improving tax compliance while maintaining accurate financial reporting.

Identification of Timing Differences

ICDS may require recognition of income or expenses at a different time than financial accounting standards. These timing differences can significantly impact taxable income if not properly identified and reported.

We assist in analysing ICDS implications relating to:

Revenue recognition.

Construction and long-term contracts.

Inventory valuation.

Borrowing costs.

Government grants.

Foreign exchange fluctuations.

Provisions and contingent liabilities.

Other ICDS-specific recognition principles.

Our detailed analysis helps businesses identify and manage timing differences effectively.

Impact Analysis on Taxable Income

ICDS adjustments may influence the amount of taxable income reported during a financial year. We perform a comprehensive impact assessment to quantify these adjustments and help businesses understand their tax implications before filing returns.

Our analysis includes:

Computation of ICDS adjustments.

Comparison between accounting profit and taxable income.

Assessment of additional tax liability, if any.

Evaluation of cash flow implications arising from ICDS compliance.

Advisory on tax planning opportunities within the applicable legal framework.

Support During Scrutiny & Tax Assessments

Questions relating to ICDS often arise during income tax assessments and scrutiny proceedings. Our professionals provide complete assistance in explaining accounting treatments, preparing supporting documentation, and responding to queries raised by tax authorities.

Our services include:

Preparation of explanations and supporting documents.

Assistance in responding to assessment notices.

Representation before Income Tax Authorities.

Clarification of ICDS-related adjustments during scrutiny proceedings.

Advisory for resolving disputes arising from income computation issues.

Benefits of ICDS Compliance

Proper implementation of Income Computation and Disclosure Standards offers several long-term benefits for businesses and professionals.

Accurate computation of taxable income.

Consistency in tax reporting across financial years.

Reduced risk of tax adjustments and reassessments.

Improved preparedness during scrutiny assessments.

Lower exposure to interest, penalties, and litigation.

Better alignment between accounting records and tax computations.

Enhanced confidence in tax compliance and reporting.

Effective tax planning is an essential part of sound financial management. At Ritesh Arora & Associates, we provide comprehensive Personal Tax Planning services tailored to your income structure, investments, financial objectives, and tax profile. Our professionals analyse your financial position and recommend tax-efficient strategies that maximise available deductions, exemptions, and benefits while ensuring complete compliance with the latest tax regulations.

Our proactive approach helps you make informed financial decisions, minimise tax exposure, and avoid unnecessary tax disputes.

Our Personal Tax Planning Services

Salary Structuring & Tax Optimisation

An efficiently structured salary package can significantly reduce your tax liability without affecting your overall compensation. We assist employees and employers in designing tax-efficient salary structures that comply with applicable tax laws while maximising available exemptions and allowances.

Our services include:

Tax-efficient salary restructuring.

Optimisation of House Rent Allowance (HRA).

Leave Travel Allowance (LTA) planning.

Structuring of allowances and reimbursements.

Advisory on taxable perquisites and employee benefits.

Review of salary components under the old and new tax regimes.

Our objective is to help you maximise your take-home income while remaining fully compliant with tax regulations.

Investment Planning under Sections 80C, 80D, 80G & Other Tax Provisions

Investing wisely not only supports your long-term financial goals but also helps reduce your taxable income. We provide strategic guidance on selecting suitable tax-saving investments based on your financial objectives, risk appetite, and eligibility under various provisions of the Income Tax Act.

Our advisory covers:

Tax-saving investments under Section 80C.

National Pension System (NPS) benefits.

Public Provident Fund (PPF).

Equity Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS).

Life insurance policies.

Health insurance deductions under Section 80D.

Donations eligible under Section 80G.

Other applicable deductions and exemptions.

We ensure your investment decisions align with both your financial goals and tax planning objectives.

Capital Gains Tax Planning

Selling property, shares, mutual funds, or other capital assets can result in significant tax implications. Proper planning before executing a transaction helps minimise tax liability and maximise available exemptions.

Our services include:

Computation of short-term and long-term capital gains.

Advisory on exemptions under Sections 54, 54F, and 54EC.

Guidance on indexation benefits wherever applicable.

Tax planning for property sales and investments.

Advisory on taxation of shares, mutual funds, and securities.

Planning for reinvestment to reduce capital gains tax.

Our professionals help structure your transactions in a tax-efficient manner while ensuring compliance with applicable laws.

Tax Planning under the Old vs New Tax Regime

The introduction of the new tax regime has made tax planning more complex for many taxpayers. Choosing the right regime depends on your income, deductions, exemptions, and overall financial profile.

We assist you by:

Comparing tax liability under both tax regimes.

Analysing eligible deductions and exemptions.

Evaluating long-term tax savings.

Advising on the most beneficial tax regime.

Reviewing tax implications annually based on changing income patterns.

Our personalised approach ensures you choose the option that delivers the maximum tax benefit.

Handling Income Tax Notices & Assessments

Receiving a notice from the Income Tax Department can be stressful, but timely professional assistance can simplify the process considerably. We provide complete support in understanding the notice, preparing appropriate responses, and representing clients before tax authorities wherever required.

Our services include:

Review and analysis of Income Tax notices.

Preparation of legally compliant responses.

Assistance during scrutiny and reassessment proceedings.

Representation before Income Tax Authorities.

Advisory on corrective actions and future compliance.

Our goal is to resolve tax matters efficiently while protecting your interests.

A structured tax planning strategy provides both immediate and long-term financial advantages.

Minimise tax liability through lawful tax-saving opportunities.

Maximise eligible deductions and exemptions.

Make informed investment decisions.

Ensure complete compliance with the Income Tax Act.

1.2.3.4.plainBody:
Errors in assessment orders, tax computations, TDS credits, or return processing can lead to incorrect tax demands or delays in receiving eligible refunds. The Income Tax Act provides taxpayers with various remedies, including rectification and revision, to correct such errors and ensure that taxes are assessed fairly. Timely action is essential to prevent unnecessary financial burden and safeguard your legal rights.

At Ritesh Arora & Associates, we assist individuals, businesses, and organisations in filing rectification and revision applications, resolving refund-related issues, and addressing discrepancies affecting tax credits. Our professionals carefully review each case and provide practical solutions to help clients recover eligible refunds and correct procedural errors efficiently.

Our Rectification, Revision & Refund Services

Filing Rectification Applications

Rectification applications are filed to correct apparent mistakes in assessment orders, intimation notices, or tax computations that may have resulted in incorrect tax demands or denial of eligible benefits.

Our services include:

Filing rectification applications before the appropriate authority.

Correction of errors in assessment orders and intimations.

Review of tax computations and demand calculations.

Preparation of supporting documents and submissions.

Revision Applications Before Appropriate Authorities

Where an assessment order is prejudicial or requires reconsideration, revision applications may provide an appropriate remedy under the Income Tax Act.

We assist in:

Evaluating eligibility for revision.

Drafting revision petitions.

Preparation of supporting legal submissions.

Representation before the relevant authorities.

Refund Tracking & Follow-Up

Delays in refund processing can occur due to verification issues, mismatches, or procedural deficiencies. We actively monitor refund status and coordinate with the Income Tax Department to facilitate timely resolution.

Our services include:

Refund status monitoring.

Follow-up with tax authorities.

Resolution of refund processing issues.

Assistance with refund-related notices and communications.

Interest on Refund Claims

Taxpayers may be entitled to interest on delayed refunds under applicable provisions of the Income Tax Act. We review refund calculations to ensure that all eligible interest has been correctly computed.

Our assistance includes:

Verification of refund interest calculations.

Review of refund orders.

Representation for incorrect or omitted interest.

Follow-up for pending refund payments.

Correction of TDS Mismatches & Credit Issues

Mismatch in TDS records or missing tax credits can adversely impact tax liability and refund eligibility. Our professionals help identify and resolve these discrepancies through proper reconciliation and follow-up.

We assist in:

Reconciliation of Form 26AS and AIS.

Resolution of TDS credit mismatches.

Coordination with deductors for correction statements.

Updating tax records to reflect accurate credits.

Benefits of Professional Rectification & Refund Assistance

Timely correction of tax-related errors.

Faster resolution of refund-related issues.

Accurate reconciliation of tax credits.

Proper representation before tax authorities.

Reduced risk of unnecessary tax demands.

Improved compliance with statutory procedures.

1.2.7.1.body:
Our Tax Audit Services for Businesses

Applicability Assessment & Turnover Threshold Evaluation

The first step in every tax audit is determining whether the audit provisions apply to the business based on turnover, gross receipts, cash transactions, and other prescribed conditions.

Our assessment includes:

  1. Evaluation of turnover and gross receipts.
  2. Review of prescribed audit thresholds.
  3. Analysis of cash receipt and payment ratios.
  4. Applicability under presumptive taxation provisions, where relevant.

Comprehensive Examination of Books of Accounts

A detailed review of financial records helps ensure that the books of accounts accurately reflect the business's financial position.

We examine:

  1. Sales and purchase registers.
  2. Ledger accounts and journal entries.
  3. Trial balance and financial statements.
  4. Revenue recognition practices.
  5. Classification of capital and revenue expenditure.
  6. Inventory and stock valuation records.

Verification of Statutory Compliance

We review statutory compliances to ensure consistency across various tax and regulatory filings.

Our review includes:

  1. TDS deductions and return filings.
  2. Reconciliation of Form 26AS and AIS.
  3. GST return reconciliation with financial statements.
  4. Advance tax and self-assessment tax payments.
  5. Verification of statutory dues such as PF, ESI, and other applicable compliances.

Identification of Disallowances & Reporting Adjustments

Our audit identifies transactions that may require reporting or adjustment under the Income Tax Act.

We review:

  1. Expenses liable for disallowance.
  2. Cash payments exceeding prescribed limits.
  3. Interest and related party transactions.
  4. Specified payments requiring disclosure.
  5. Other reporting adjustments under applicable tax provisions.

Review of Related Party Transactions & Specified Payments

Certain transactions require additional disclosures under the tax audit report.

We assist in reviewing:

  1. Related party transactions.
  2. Specified domestic transactions.
